newsitem.title: USA: Henkel says still interested in negotiated deal with Loctite.
newsitem.headline: Henkel says still interested in negotiated deal with Loctite.

text.p: Henkel KGaA said Tuesday it was disappointed at Loctite Corp.'s decision spurning its $1.2 billion bid, but remained interested in reaching a deal.

Henkel's response to a Loctite special committee's decision to not recommend acceptance of the $57.75-a-share offer to Loctite shareholders was contained in a letter the German company sent to the panel Tuesday.
A copy of the letter to the Hartford, Conn.,-based speciality adhesives maker was attached to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The letter was signed by Henkel President Hans Dietrich.
In the letter signed by Henkel President hans Dietrich, the company said it was prepared to meet with the special committee and its advisers promptly to accomplish its goal of a negotiated deal.

Henkel, which made the bid for the 65 percent stake in the company it does not already own, said Loctite's decision to seek a buyer was an "important step" in furthering the interests of shareholders.
The German chemicals and consumer products company said it expected to be contacted by Loctite's advisers, who were instructed by the U.S. company to contact potential buyers.

Henkel said it expected to be provided the same information made available by Loctite to other interested parties. It said it should be given a "reasonable opportunity" to respond to any competing offer.

It also said it would be inappropriate for Loctite, if the U.S. company should accept an acquisition proposal from a third party, to agree to any "break-up fee" or accept options or similar "lock-up" arrangements" that might be designed to preclude a response from Henkel.

On Monday, Loctite announced that a special committee of its board had determined that Henkel's bid was inadequate, and that the committee had determined "to seek to sell the company at a price that fully reflected its value."
Loctite stock closed at $60, up 12.5 cents in trading at the New York Stock exchange.
